a.xlink:title: Generate IMG-RAD-07 photometric performance simulations, one set per requirement, as set in the scenario config.
a.text: per requirement, as set in the

a.xlink:title:
Stub for METIS-2594: METIS internal calibration shall provide a range of flux levels matching that encountered in scientific operation as defined in METIS-3137.
Writes nothing (the scenario's cases are still checked, so the config stays valid for a future implementation).
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files (empty)
a.text: a range of flux levels matching

a.xlink:title:
Simulated data for METIS-2883: the source used for detector linearity calibration shall provide an illumination that is spatially homogeneous within +/- 3% peak-to-valley over the science field of view.
Per case, a full-aperture ScopeSim flat with a smooth illumination pattern injected so that max |pixel / mean - 1| = injected half_ptv (on top of whatever inhomogeneity ScopeSim itself produces). Writes one PASS case and one FAIL case (and e.g. one near the limit, if configured).
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files

Simulated data for METIS-3300: the level of flux of the flat field shall be tunable to 15 discrete values and shall be known at each step to 0.3%; the resulting spatial illumination pattern shall remain constant across the field within 0.5% after tuning.
Flux steps: the WCU black-body aperture is fixed (bb_aperture); the exposure E = T_ND x DIT is stepped linearly, E_k = E_max * k / n_steps (header NOMFLUX = k / n_steps, the nominal relative flux). E_max puts the raw peak (background included, which scales with E too) at sim_common.MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation / (1 + peak_margin), scaled from the probe ctx.lit_frame() (base ND and DIT). Per step, the least attenuating ND of nd_filters with DIT = E_k / T_ND >= the detector's minimum DIT is used (choose_nd_and_dit), with two darks and a flat read out at that ND and DIT (the background scales with it). Per case and step, injected: - flux error: the flux is off the nominal by +/- flux_error (alternating sign), - pattern change: a smooth pattern with amplitude ramping from -pattern_change to +pattern_change over the steps (so each step's normalised flat differs from the step-averaged one by at most pattern_change). Writes ..._<case>_stepNN.fits for one PASS case and one FAIL case (more if configured), one ScopeSim readout per step shared by all cases.
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files
a.text: level of flux of the flat field

a.xlink:title:
Simulated data for METIS-3291: METIS shall allow the characterisation and correction of the relative spectral response function (RSRF) with 3% precision over the wavelength range specified in METIS-1090.
Needs an LSS instrument set-up (wcu_lss_l/m/n). From the un-injected ScopeSim signal (lit frame - dark_1), with the naming of modules/rsrf_common.py: - wavelength per pixel from ScopeSim's spectral trace, and S_empirical, the sum over the illuminated slit columns per row, - S_perfect: the BB at the WCU temperature (unit throughput and QE), scaled so its integral is src_scale_factor x that of S_empirical, - alpha_fcn: the observing filter's smoothed ripple, scaled so that integral(S_perfect * alpha_fcn) = alpha_integral_frac x integral(S_perfect), - the reference RSRF, RSRF_REF = S_empirical / (S_perfect * alpha_fcn). The RSRF is evaluated on the rows inside the trace's range and the filter passband (standing in for the METIS-1090 range). Per case, the signal is multiplied by (1 + rsrf_error * P(lambda)), P a smooth pattern in wavelength with mean 0 and max |P| = 1 over the evaluated rows (rsrf_error_pattern), so the RSRF measured from the case file deviates from RSRF_REF by max |rsrf / RSRF_REF - 1| = rsrf_error (plus noise; rsrf_deviation). Each case file gets an 'RSRF' table extension (rsrf_table) with the wavelength solution, the model and the reference and true RSRFs, for the ANALYSIS. Writes one PASS case and one FAIL case (more if configured).
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files

The project root (METIS_MAIT_code_eckhart/), as set in config/paths.yaml.

a.xlink:title:
Run the requirement simulators of a scenario config: for each instrument, one OpticalTrain, with the DIT shortened if needed so the raw readout (aperture fully open) peaks at <= MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation (limit_dit_to_saturation); for each requirement with simulate: true that applies to it, the requirement's simulator, simulator(ctx, req_key, req_cfg) -> list of written files, with req_cfg resolved for the instrument's detector (see resolve_for_detector).
INPUTS: - scenario (dict): the scenario config - simulators (dict): requirement key -> simulator function - observing (dict): merged observing config (common + test-specific) - out_dir (str): directory to write to - test_prefix (str): file name prefix, e.g. 'IMG_OPT_04' - plot_dir (str or None): directory for FYI plots (ctx.plot_dir), if any; see sim_plot_dir
OUTPUTS: - dict: (requirement key, instrument name) -> list of written files

Load the common observing config, then merge each test-specific config on top, in order (top-level keys of later files override earlier ones).
INPUTS ---------- stem : str Project root (METIS_MAIT_code_eckhart/), prepended to relative paths. *test_config_files : str Test-specific observing configs, relative to stem or absolute.
OUTPUTS ------- dict The merged observing config.

Load a YAML configuration file and pipe its contents to the log.
INPUTS ---------- config_file_choice : str Path to the configuration file. print_one_line : bool, optional If True, log the entire config on a single line. If False (default), log in a more readable, multiline format.
OUTPUTS ------- config_this : dict The configuration dictionary loaded from file.
a.text: Load a YAML configuration file and
pipe its contents to the log

a.xlink:title:
Check the cases of a requirement: a 'pass' and a 'fail' case exist, every case injects every limited quantity, and the 'pass'/'fail' cases are on the right side of the limit. Exits otherwise.
OUTPUTS: - dict: case name -> EXPECTED ('PASS' or 'FAIL')

Largest exposure E = T_ND x DIT (s) for which the raw peak (background included, which also scales with T_ND x DIT) stays at max_raw / (1 + margin), from a probe readout peaking at peak_raw with ND transmission t_probe and DIT dit_probe.
Raises ValueError if the probe has no positive peak.

ND filter and DIT giving an exposure T_ND x DIT: the least attenuating ND (highest transmission) for which DIT = exposure / T_ND is >= mindit, so the DIT stays legal.
INPUTS: - exposure (float): T_ND x DIT (s) - nd_transmissions (dict): ND name -> transmission - mindit (float): minimum DIT (s)
OUTPUTS: - str: ND name - float: DIT (s)
Raises ValueError if even the most attenuating ND needs DIT < mindit.

a.xlink:title: Observe with the WCU black-body aperture at bb_aperture; read out one frame.
Put ND filter `filter` (one of the ND wheel's, e.g. 'ND_OD3') in the beam.
Two independent darks (black-body aperture closed): dark_1 to extract the signal from the illuminated frames, dark_2 to write out as BACKGROUND.

Write one case: primary header (ScopeSim's + set-up + requirement cards), then BCKGD_SUBTED (raw - background), RAW_READOUT and BACKGROUND, as float32, then extra_hdus (astropy HDUs, written as given). If saturation_adu is given, the header also gets SAT_ADU and PEAKFRAC (max of the raw readout / saturation), and a warning is logged if PEAKFRAC > MAX_RAW_FRAC.
OUTPUTS: - str: path of the written file

Smooth pattern P(lambda) for the METIS-3291 injection: a tilt, a curvature and a slow wave in x = lambda scaled to [-1, 1] over lam_eval_um (the rows the RSRF is evaluated on; x is clipped outside them), with mean 0 and max |P| = 1 over lam_eval_um, so that an RSRF times (1 + a * P) deviates from the original by at most a there.
INPUTS: - lam_um (ndarray): wavelengths to evaluate P at [um] (any shape) - lam_eval_um (ndarray): wavelengths of the evaluated rows [um]
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: P, the shape of lam_um
a.text: curvature and a slow wave in x =

a.xlink:title: The quantity METIS-3291 is tested on: max |rsrf / rsrf_ref - 1| over the evaluated rows (what the SIM injects as rsrf_error).

RSRF extension (one row per detector row): the wavelength solution, the un-injected S_empirical, the model (S_perfect, alpha_fcn), the reference RSRF and the injected (true) RSRF of the case.
INPUTS: - spec (rsrf_common.SlitSpectrum): of the un-injected signal - evaluate (ndarray): bool per row, RSRF evaluated there - model (dict): s_perfect, alpha, rsrf_ref (per row) - pattern_rows (ndarray): rsrf_error_pattern per row - rsrf_error (float): injected amplitude
OUTPUTS: - fits.BinTableHDU: EXTNAME 'RSRF'

FYI plot of the METIS-3291 simulation: left, S_empirical (un-injected), S_perfect and S_perfect * alpha_fcn; right, the reference RSRF (RSRF_REF).
INPUTS: - plot_dir (str): where to write fyi_sim_<label>.png - label (str): e.g. 'METIS-3291_L_spec' - spec (rsrf_common.SlitSpectrum), model (dict): see rsrf_table
OUTPUTS: - str: path of the written plot

Wavelength and slit position of every detector pixel, from the first spectral trace of the OpticalTrain.
INPUTS: - metis (OpticalTrain): in an LSS mode (with a 'spectral_traces' effect) - shape (tuple): (ny, nx) of the detector frame - det_key (str): 'img_lm' or 'img_n' (selects the detector layout file) - irdb_dir (str): IRDB location
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: wavelength per pixel [um] - ndarray: slit position xi per pixel [arcsec] - trace: the ScopeSim spectral trace used (wave_min, wave_max, trace_id)

Slit-collapsed spectrum: the sum over the illuminated columns (slit_columns), with each row's median slit wavelength; rows are flagged in_range if inside [wave_min, wave_max] (no extrapolation of the trace).
OUTPUTS: - SlitSpectrum
Filter curve file of obs_filter (polychromatic_observing_filters_<band>_...).

Ripple of a filter curve: (curve, lightly smoothed) / (its broad in-band trend), taken in the passband (T > in_band_frac x max(T)) and 1 outside it. The trend is a normalized convolution of the in-band samples only, so the band edges don't pull it down; in_band_frac ~0.9 keeps the steep edges out of the ripple.
INPUTS: - filter_file (Path): table with columns wavelength [um], transmission - ripple_sigma_um (float): light smoothing (keeps the ripple, removes noise) - trend_sigma_um (float): broad smoothing (the trend divided out) - in_band_frac (float): passband threshold, as a fraction of max(T)
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: filter wavelengths [um] - ndarray: ripple (~1 in band, 1 outside) - ndarray: bool, in the passband
a.text: band trend), taken in the passband

a.xlink:title: Rows on which the RSRF is evaluated: inside the trace's wavelength range and in the filter passband (stands in for the METIS-1090 wavelength range).
a.text: Rows on which the RSRF is
wavelength range and in the filter

a.xlink:title:
Black-body spectrum through a system of unit throughput and QE, in ADU per row: B_ph(lam, T) * area * pixel solid angle * n_cols * dlam per row * exptime / gain (1 photon = 1 e-). Not included: BB emissivity, BB -> integrating-sphere coupling and gain, BB aperture, the sphere's own thermal emission.
INPUTS: - lam_rows_um (ndarray): wavelength per row [um] (all rows, so the row widths np.gradient(lam_rows_um) are defined everywhere) - bb_temp (Quantity or float): BB temperature [K] - area, pixel_scale: Quantities (or floats in m2, arcsec), e.g. from metis.cmds['!TEL.area'], metis.cmds['!INST.pixel_scale'] - gain (float): e- / ADU - n_cols (int): number of slit columns summed - exptime_s (float): DIT x NDIT [s]
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: ADU per row
a.text: system of unit throughput and QE,
in ADU per row: B_ph(lam, T) *

a.xlink:title:
S_perfect: s_unit scaled so that sum(S_perfect) = factor x sum(s_empirical) (sums over the rows given).
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: S_perfect - float: the scale applied

alpha_fcn(lambda) = alpha_scale x ripple(lambda), with alpha_scale such that sum(S_perfect * alpha_fcn) = integral_frac x sum(S_perfect) over the rows lam_um.
OUTPUTS: - callable: alpha_fcn(lam_um) - float: alpha_scale
rsrf = S_empirical / (S_perfect * alpha_fcn).

a.text: PSF kernel set, IPC on or off)

a.xlink:title: Saturation level (ADU per DIT) from the observing config, or None: that of obs_mode in saturation_adu_by_obs_mode (modes whose detector readout mode differs from the imaging default, e.g. the LSS modes), else that of the detector in saturation_adu.
Detector key ('img_lm' or 'img_n') of a WCU imaging obs_mode.

Shorten the DIT, if needed, so that the peak of the raw readout (aperture fully open) is <= max_frac * saturation_adu. Never lengthens it.
Each trial takes a dark and an illuminated readout at the current DIT. If the raw peak is too high, the DIT is rescaled to aim at target_frac * saturation, assuming the signal is linear in DIT on top of the dark level: dit_new = dit * (target_frac * sat - median(dark)) / (peak - median(dark)), at most halving the DIT per trial if the peak is at saturation (the readout may be clipped there, which makes the linear estimate too optimistic). The readouts are per DIT (ScopeSim averages over NDIT), so NDIT is left as it is; the trials use trial_ndit (default 1: quick, and the noisier peak errs on the safe side; None for the configured NDIT).
INPUTS: - metis: OpticalTrain - instrument (dict): instrument config, with 'dit' and 'ndit' (not modified) - saturation_adu (float): saturation level (ADU per DIT) - max_frac, target_frac (float): limit and aim for the raw peak, as fractions of saturation - max_iter (int): maximum number of trials - readout_fn: readout function, readout_fn(metis, bb_aperture, instrument) -> (frame, header); injectable for tests - trial_ndit (int or None): NDIT of the trial readouts
OUTPUTS: - dict: a copy of instrument with 'dit' set to the tuned DIT - dict: dit_cfg, dit, peak_frac (raw peak / saturation of the last trial), n_trials
Raises ValueError if the dark level alone is >= target_frac * saturation, and RuntimeError if no DIT within max_iter trials is short enough.
a.text: Shorten the DIT, if needed, so
that the peak of the raw readout
